label: SYNTHETIC. Fictional guidance written for the Lumen portfolio demo. Not a real reinsurer manual and not medical or underwriting advice.

passages.title: Referral thresholds
passages.text: A sum assured above EUR 750,000, any decline, and any case that hard-stops for insufficient evidence requires second-level review and co-signature, regardless of the rating outcome.

passages.title: Conditions not covered by this manual
passages.text: Where this manual has no section for a condition, the case must not be rated by analogy to a different condition. Such cases are referred to the medical officer, and any rating requires specific evidence for that condition.

passages.title: Cancer history: general approach
passages.text: A history of malignancy is rated on three factors: stage at diagnosis, time since completion of active treatment, and evidence of continued remission. No cover is offered while treatment is ongoing. Cases are rated from the date treatment was completed, not the date of diagnosis.

passages.title: Breast cancer, stage I
passages.text: For stage I breast cancer, time since completion of treatment sets the rating. Under 2 years: postpone. 2 to under 3 years: loading of 100%. 3 to under 5 years: loading of 50%. 5 years or more with no recurrence and clear surveillance: standard rates, loading of 0%.

passages.title: Breast cancer, stage II and above
passages.text: Stage II or higher is outside the pre-validated bands. Cases at 7 or more years from treatment with clear surveillance may be considered at a loading of 25% to 75%, but every such case requires medical officer review before a rating is confirmed.

passages.title: Evidence required for a cancer rating
passages.text: A rating under section 4 requires the pathology summary, the treating oncologist report confirming stage and completion date, and the most recent surveillance result. Any recurrence, metastasis or new primary at any time moves the case to decline or medical officer referral.

passages.title: Hypertension
passages.text: Average readings under 140/90 on no more than two medications: standard rates. Average readings of 140-159 over 90-99: loading of 25%. Readings of 160/100 or above: loading of 50% and medical officer review.

passages.title: Myocardial infarction
passages.text: Under 12 months from the event: postpone. 1 to 3 years: loading of 100%. Over 3 years with a normal recent stress test: loading of 50%. Any cardiac event requires medical officer review.

passages.title: Type 2 diabetes, uncomplicated
passages.text: HbA1c of 7.0% or below with no complications: loading of 25%. HbA1c of 7.1% to 8.5%: loading of 50%. Rated from the average of the last two results.

passages.title: Diabetes with complications
passages.text: Any evidence of retinopathy, nephropathy or neuropathy, or an HbA1c above 8.5%: loading of 100% and medical officer review. Declined if more than one complication is present.

passages.title: Hazardous occupations
passages.text: Offshore and work-at-height occupations: loading of 25%. Underground mining: loading of 50%. Occupational loadings are added to, not substituted for, any medical loading.

passages.title: Hazardous pursuits
passages.text: Recreational flying, motor racing and mountaineering above 4,000 metres are rated individually and referred to the underwriting manager when combined with any medical loading.
